statement: The ordinary Dirichlet series sum n^(-s) converges only for Re(s)>1; analytic continuation does not make its ordinary partial sums converge in the critical strip.
For real t, Hardy Z(t) is real and Z(t)=0 iff zeta(1/2+it)=0.
A strictly signed interval enclosure for Z(t) certifies its sign; opposite strict endpoint signs imply at least one zero by continuity.
A sign change alone cannot establish exact isolation or completeness because even-multiplicity zeros may be missed.
If a complete critical-line certificate yields N0(T)=m and an independent rigorous count yields N(T)=m, then every nontrivial zero through T lies on the critical line.
A bounded certificate through T proves no statement above T.
Global RH is equivalent to the universal obligation forall T>0, N0(T)=N(T).
next_test: Bind exact definitions and equivalence in Lean/Mathlib.

statement: A zeta zero in 0<sigma<=1 can be represented by ordinary partial sums sum_{n<=N} n^(-s) tending to zero.
failure: Ordinary Dirichlet partial sums do not converge to analytic continuation in the critical strip.

statement: If positive weighted vectors have partial sums tending to zero, a nonvanishing proportion of weight lies outside every closed semicircle.
failure: The proof moves from negligible mass outside a closed semicircle to positive mass in a shrunken inner arc; boundary mass is uncontrolled. Signed boundary constructions with weights tending to zero can converge while all phases remain on the semicircle boundary.
next_test: Reformulate using an open semicircle with a uniform angular margin, or normalized resultant bounds.

statement: Semicircle exclusion yields two persistent angular regions with fixed positive mass proportions.
failure: Depends on C011; partition constants and quantifier order require repair.

statement: Two persistent regions must have angular separation bounded below because otherwise their union lies in a semicircle.
failure: The intervals are fixed after extraction, so their distance does not tend with k. A fixed positive mass inside a semicircle does not contradict a claim that only some positive mass must lie outside it.
next_test: State a quantitative resultant lemma using total outside mass and vector projection.

statement: Cancellation forces two dominant regional vectors to approach opposition.
failure: The remainder is only known to have less than total mass by a fixed proportion; no inequality shows it is smaller than the lower bound for the sum of the two selected vectors.
next_test: Derive explicit constants c1,c2 and a strict remainder bound; search finite counterexamples.

statement: Any weighted phase configuration contains a directionally coherent subset with a fixed mass/projection fraction.
failure: The paper alternates between a projection lower bound and a mass lower bound; the stated 1/pi consequence is not reconstructed from the extracted equations.
next_test: Use averaging over semicircles: some semicircle contains at least half total mass; separately prove projection bound 1/pi or 2/pi with exact normalization.

statement: A lower bound on weighted projection implies fixed positive mass in a narrower angular sector.
next_test: Recover exact constants eta and threshold and formalize Markov-style estimate.

statement: A substantial cluster forces a comparably substantial near-opposite cluster.
failure: Applying a generic coherence lemma to the complement does not force the selected coherent subset to align with the complement resultant; the projection argument lacks a budget over all remaining mass.
next_test: Formulate vector-measure decomposition theorem or produce finite counterexample.

statement: Near-opposing clusters allow extraction of an increasing subsequence whose successive phase gaps are pi plus uniformly bounded errors with bound <pi.
failure: Cluster recurrence does not imply alternation of individual terms with the required mass or preserve cancellation in the extracted subseries.
next_test: Specify selection map and prove subseries relevance without rearrangement.

statement: Cancellation of a full convergent series forces cancellation/convergence of the extracted alternating subseries.
failure: A subseries of a conditionally convergent series need not converge to the same value and may diverge; extraction requires an independent remainder theorem.
next_test: Provide a decomposition identity with controlled complementary residual.

statement: Convergence of an alternating perturbed subseries forces consecutive magnitudes to become equal.
failure: Convergence forces individual terms to zero, not generally pairwise cancellation. Exact hypotheses and inequality are missing from text extraction.
next_test: Recover formula from DOCX and test against convergent non-pairwise examples.

statement: For a_n=n_k^(-sigma), asymptotic equality of consecutive magnitudes implies n_{k+1}/n_k -> 1.
If n_{k+1}/n_k ->1 then t log(n_{k+1}/n_k)->0 for fixed t.
The extracted alternating envelope forces those same real phase increments to remain bounded away from zero.
failure: Depends on unproved alternating subsequence extraction and branch-unwrapping.

statement: Every convergent complex series with sum zero must exhibit local consecutive pair cancellation.
failure: Counterexample: -1 + sum_{n>=1} 2^(-n)=0 converges, but positive tail terms do not cancel consecutively.

statement: Strictly decreasing block magnitudes cannot sum to zero because no later block can cancel an earlier block.
failure: Strict decrease is insufficient; a first vector can equal the vector sum of a decreasing tail, e.g. 0.5-0.3-0.2=0.

statement: Monotone unbounded phases with increments tending to zero imply phase values are dense modulo 2pi.
next_test: Formal epsilon-crossing proof; monotonicity and exact unboundedness must be retained.

statement: Density/sign changes prevent directional convergence of the weighted sum.
failure: Infinite sign changes and dense phases do not by themselves preclude convergence; coefficient decay and cancellation rates are decisive.
next_test: State a quantitative lower-bound hypothesis on coherent-window weights.

statement: A scale-consistent residual return requires invariance of a curvature-rotation ratio under every fixed scaling.
failure: Scale invariance is asserted as necessary for a global zero but no theorem connects residual closure to invariance of the chosen local ratio.
next_test: Search counterexamples among analytic paths with exact returns but non-scale-invariant local curvature.

statement: Functional-equation symmetry about 1/2 forces each zero individually onto the symmetry axis.
failure: Reflection symmetry permits off-axis pairs; symmetry of a zero set does not imply every point is fixed by the symmetry.

statement: An off-line realization requires extra variance information and therefore is not native to the RH branch.
failure: Information classification does not eliminate analytic zeros; branch membership is not a zero-free theorem.

statement: The finite-measure identity for truncated sums and positivity/ordered-support properties are exact.
The ideal geometric alternating exponential series sums to 1/(1+e^-alpha)>0.
A zero forces an exponentially spaced dominant subsequence with exponentially decaying rounding corrections.
failure: No valid implication from global cancellation to a single dominant exponential subsequence has survived; integer rounding error decay alone does not establish dominance or exhaust other mass.
next_test: Construct exact decomposition with a bounded residual, not only a selected subsequence.

statement: The original paper proves off-line nonvanishing and hence RH.
failure: Multiple essential dependencies are refuted or unproved, and the primary analytic carrier is invalid.

statement: A corrected full solve could proceed by proving a legitimate global off-line exclusion for completed zeta/xi or by proving forall T, N0(T)=N(T).
next_test: Formalize the bounded theorem and test salvageable geometric lemmas against completed-zeta or Hardy-Z identities.
